title.purpose: The page name in the top bar; the empty-state lead uses it at 500.

transcript.purpose: The words in the bubbles; the live status line uses it at 500.

body.purpose: The base: inputs, the alert, empty-state copy and the timer.

body-strong.purpose: Buttons, top-bar links, segment labels and action labels.

label.purpose: Pane headings and the Latest pill.

small.purpose: The subtitle beside the page name and the detail line under an action.

caption.purpose: Speaker names above a run of lines, and the language chip.

meta.purpose: Timestamps, counts and the call-ended line, in tabular figures.

shadows.name: pane
shadows.purpose: The console only (light mode), always paired with the glass highlight.

shadows.name: button
shadows.purpose: The ink-filled primary button and the Latest pill (light mode).

shadows.name: button-dark
shadows.purpose: The primary button and the Latest pill in dark mode.

shadows.name: glass-highlight
shadows.purpose: 1px inner top highlight (Shine) on glass, light mode. Glass pairs it with a 28px backdrop blur on the console and 16px on the Latest pill.

shadows.name: glass-highlight-dark
shadows.purpose: The inner top highlight in dark mode.

shadows.name: segment-lift
shadows.purpose: The selected language segment; the inset uses Shine (rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07) in dark mode).

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: state changes, rises, the press and the speaking ripple.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Hover and selection: colour, fill, border and the segment lift.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: New transcript lines, action rows, the alert and the call-ended line; the Latest pill rises in 180ms.

motion.name: draft-settle
motion.purpose: A draft line fills in (fill, border, colour) when the final transcript lands.

motion.name: voice-follow
motion.purpose: The discs follow the live voice level, up to scale 1.12 and full opacity.

motion.name: blink-waiting
motion.purpose: Hollow status dot while connecting or waiting for Giulia.

motion.name: blink-thinking
motion.purpose: Solid status dot while she thinks.

motion.name: ripple-speaking
motion.value: 1.4s infinite, ring from scale 0.6 at opacity 0.9 to scale 1.6 at opacity 0
motion.purpose: Ring around the status dot while she speaks.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animations off; discs change opacity only (0.4s linear, resting 0.4)
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Scrolling jumps instead of moving smoothly.

components.css: .ds-booth { position: relative; isolation: isolate; overflow: hidden; padding: 48px 40px; background: var(--ground, #f0f0f0); color: var(--ink, #0b0b0b); font: 400 14px/1.5 ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-disc { position: absolute; z-index: -1; border-radius: 50%; pointer-events: none; } .ds-disc::before, .ds-disc::after { content: ""; position: absolute; border: 1px solid var(--ring, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.09)); border-radius: 50%; } .ds-disc::before { inset: -7%; } .ds-disc::after { inset: -16%; opacity: 0.6; } .ds-disc-her { top: -60px; left: -40px; width: 220px; height: 220px; background: var(--light-her, #d4d4d4); opacity: 0.85; } .ds-disc-you { right: -40px; bottom: -70px; width: 190px; height: 190px; background: var(--light-you, #bcbcbc); opacity: 0.7; } .ds-console { min-height: 160px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--edge, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.07)); border-radius: 20px; background: linear-gradient(160deg, var(--sheen, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)), transparent 38%), var(--glass, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.42)); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(28px); backdrop-filter: blur(28px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 var(--shine, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85)), 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04), 0 32px 64px -32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); } .ds-console-head { padding: 16px 20px 4px; color: var(--ink-2, #3d3d3d); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-console-body { margin: 0; padding: 8px 20px 20px; } @supports not ((backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) or (-webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(1px))) { .ds-console { background: var(--glass-solid, #f3f3f3); } }

narrative.overview:
Talk to Giulia is a call console seen through frosted glass. The conversation is the content: a teammate starts a call, hears Giulia open, and reads what she heard, what she said and what she did. Everything is monochrome, from near-black to white with no tint, so the only things that pull the eye are the lines being spoken and the one action that matters now.

The glass has a job. Behind the console sit two crisp discs with hairline rings, Giulia's across its top-left corner and yours across its bottom-right, and each swells with its speaker's live voice level. They are sharp outside the glass and frosted behind it, and that contrast is what makes the glass read as glass. In dark mode the discs are lights that brighten; in light mode they are shadows that deepen. Light and dark are equal modes: the system's choice applies until the teammate picks one with the toggle.

Density is that of a working instrument on a laptop: 14px base type, 44px controls, a 69px control bar and a console that fills the window. Motion is small and functional. State changes take 180ms on one ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)), new lines rise 4px into place over 220ms, and only the voice moves continuously. The world refuses the category default: a coloured chat app with a neon voice orb, or a dashboard of cards.
keyCharacteristics: Strict neutrals: every colour has equal red, green and blue, in both modes.
One frosted console (28px blur) over the voice light; surfaces inside it are raised or hairlined, never frosted again.
Ink is the action: one ink-filled button per bar, your own words in ink, errors as a solid ink block.
State is told by shape, outline and motion, never by hue.
The platform UI face at 400, 500 and 600, with tabular figures for every time.
Lucide outline icons at a 1.75 stroke; 20px panes, 12px controls, full pills.

rules.name: The Zero Chroma Rule
rules.body: Every colour on this page has equal red, green and blue. There is no tint in the grays, no blue link, no green success and no red error. When something must stand out, it gets more ink, not a hue.

rules.name: The Ink Is the Alarm Rule
rules.body: The loudest thing this world can do is a solid block of ink. A blocked microphone, a failed join or a failed start appears as an ink-filled alert at the top of the console (a light block in dark mode), never as red.

rules.name: The Twin Token Rule
rules.body: Every colour token is defined twice, once for light and once for dark. A token with one value is unfinished. Shadows stay black in both modes; dark mode only raises their opacity.

rules.name: The Platform Face Rule
rules.body: The page uses the platform UI stack and loads no font of its own. It is a UI face for a working tool, not a display face: nothing is set larger than 16px, and a surface that wants a display voice needs a new type decision, not a bigger system font.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, duration and count is set in tabular figures, so a ticking timer and a column of timestamps never jitter.

rules.name: The Conversation First Rule
rules.body: The transcript always gets the width the 300px rail leaves, and on phones the rail goes under it. The control bar is the only thing above the conversation.

rules.name: The Blur Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Frost only what has something moving behind it: the console over the voice light (28px) and the Latest pill over scrolling lines (16px). Inputs, bubbles, segments and action rows inside the console are raised or hairlined, never frosted again.

rules.name: The Circle Is the Voice Rule
rules.body: Circles mean voice: the status dot, its ripple and the two discs with their rings. Controls are rounded rectangles or pills, never circles.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Draft Rule
rules.body: A dashed outline means "not final yet": your words as heard so far. It is used for nothing else.

rules.name: The One Ink Button Rule
rules.body: A bar holds exactly one ink-filled button: Start talking when idle and End call when live. While the browser blocks audio, Tap to hear Giulia takes the ink and End call steps down to quiet.

dos: Do take every colour from the page tokens, and give each new token both values: light on the page scope, dark under `html[data-talk-theme="dark"]`.
Do keep the pre-paint html backgrounds in `public/index.html`, and the theme colour the page sets, equal to Ground (#f0f0f0 light, #0a0a0a dark).
Do keep exactly one ink-filled button in a bar; when a more urgent action appears, the previous primary steps down to quiet.
Do tell state with fill, outline, shape and motion: a hollow dot while connecting, a dashed outline for a draft, an ink block for an error.
Do use Lucide outline icons at a 1.75 stroke (14px in links and pills, 16px in buttons, 18px in the theme toggle, alerts and action rows), always beside or labelled by text.
Do set every time, duration and count in tabular figures.
Do keep the 2px solid ink focus ring, offset 2px (1px inside the segmented control), on everything focusable.
Do honour reduced motion: stop every animation, jump instead of scrolling smoothly, and let the voice light change opacity only, from a resting 0.4.
donts: Don't introduce hue anywhere on the Talk page: no red errors, green success, blue links or tinted grays.
Don't frost a surface that has nothing moving behind it; surfaces inside the console use the raised fill or a hairline, without blur.
Don't drift back to the category default this world refuses: a coloured chat app with a neon voice orb, or a dashboard of cards.
Don't set the platform face at display sizes or give this page a webfont; the type ramp ends at 16px.
Don't lighten Third Ink (#575757 light, #9a9a9a dark); it is tuned to hold at least 4.5:1 on the frosted console in both modes, over the discs included.
Don't carry this system onto `/calls`; that page keeps its own look and its green, amber and red latency colours.
